This is a petition filed u/s.166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, claiming for compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.
2. The petitioner's case in brief as follows:

On 4-11-2017 at about 3.45 a.m. when the petitioner was riding the motor cycle Honda Activa bearing No.KA-53- H-8617 along with his friends Philip Abraham and Mahateja as pillion riders on Timber layout main road, Timber yard layout,
Bengaluru, near Rose wood international hotel, driver of the MGV bearing No.KA-53-C-4047 came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, on extreme right side of the road and dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to impact, petitioner and pillion riders sustained severe injuries and motor cycle was also damaged.

Immediately petitioner was sifted to hospital, after first aid treatment shifted to Fortis hospital, thereafter shifted to St.John's medical college hospital, Bengaluru wherein took treatment as inpatient and discharged on 12-12-2017.

The petitioner spent amount of Rs.10 lakhs for hospitalization, conveyance, medical treatment,
attendant and other incidental expenses.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.50 lakhs from the respondents.
3. In response of Tribunal process, the respondent No.1 to 3 appeared through their respective counsel and only respondent No.1 and 3 filed their respective written statement.

The respondent No.1 in its written statement contended that the driver of the lorry was very careful and had taken all precautions and it is negligence of the petitioner who was driving without observing the lorry was already was in the road by taking the right turn and petitioner who was on the wheels the accident was caused only due to the carelessness and negligent and not keeping presence of mind by the petitioner who was driving negligently driven and due to this reason the accident occurred.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.

5. The respondent No.3 in its written statement contended that the above petition is bad for non joinder of necessary and proper parties as the petitioner has failed to implead the owner and insured of the Honda Activa bearing reg.No.KA-53-H-8617.

The owner of the Honda Aciva intentionally entrusted/allowed 3 adult persons to travel on the honda activa on the road knowing fully well that the seating capacity of the honda activa is only 2, in the complaint, FIR, charge sheet and other police documents clearly reflects that at the time of accident there were three members were traveling on the honda activa.
This respondent is not necessary and proper party for the adjudication fo the above case.
The jurisdictional police have filed the charge sheet against the rider and owner of the honda activa bearing No.KA-53-H-8617.

Since there was no valid insurance policy to the honda activa, the jurisdictional police colluded with the petitioner has filed false charge sheet against the driver of the goods vehicle as A1 only with an intention to claim compensation by taking advantage of policy of insurance.
This respondent seeks protection u/s 147 & 149 of MV Act.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive.
The claim is bad for non compliance of section 158(6) and 134(c) of MV Act.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.

6. From the above said pleadings this tribunal has framed the following issues :
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the MVG bearing reg.No.KA-53-C- 4047 on 4-11-2017 at about 3.45 a.m. near rose wood international hotel, Timber yard layout,
Bengaluru ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3
. What Order or Award?

The respondent No.3 got examined its Assistant Manager as RW-1 and got marked Ex-R1 and 2.
8.
Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1:-

In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Ex-P1 to 137 documents i.e., FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, rough sketch, statement, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet, col. 133 notice,
reply, discharge summaries, medical bills, prescriptions, 3 photos, CD, aadhaar card.

11. On the other hand, counsel for the respondent No.3 has seriously disputed the cause and manner of the accident and contended that the accident has been taken place due to the sole rash and negligent driving of the motor cycle Honda Activa by the petitioner himself who was riding along with the two pillion riders.

It was argued by the learned counsel for the respondent that the petitioner was riding the Honda Activa bearing No.KA-53-H-8617 without coverage of the insurance policy and without driving licence and along with the two pillion riders in a rash and negligent manner with high speed early in the morning at 3.45 a.m. and lost control over the vehicle and dashed against the rare right wheel portion of the goods vehicle MGV bearing No.KA-53-C-4047 and fell down and sustained injuries.

Further it was argued by the learned counsel for the respondent that the complainant eyewitness has voluntarily lodge the complaint before the police authorities stating that accident has been occurred solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Activa honda who rode the same along with the two pillion riders and dashed against the rare right wheel of the goods vehicle.

Further argued that even the jurisdictional police have filed the charge sheet against the rider and owner of the Activa honda for offence punishable u/s 279, 337, 338 of IPC 128 r/w 177, 3(1) r/w 181, 146 r/w 196 of IMV Act by contending that accused No.2 rider of the motor cycle Activa honda riding the same along with two pillion riders without coverage of the insurance policy and without valid and effective driving licence and thereby caused the accident.
Further argued that since the petitioner was driving the vehicle which was not having the valid insurance policy, the petitioner colluding with the jurisdictional police and made the police to file false charge sheet against the driver of the goods vehicle as accused No.1 only with intention to claim the compensation from the respondents.
Further argued that respondent is not at all responsible for the cause of the accident.
Hence above claim petition is liable to be dismissed against this respondent.

12. In the present case, charge sheet filed against the driver of the lorry for the offence punishable u/s 279, 338 of IPC and Charge sheet filed against the petitioner rider of the motor cycle for the offence punishable u/s 128 not for 279 of IPC.

13. In this regard-The Hon'ble Apex Court in Civil Appeal No.79/2020 (Mohammed Siddiqui & Anr.,
v. National Insurance Co. Ltd., & Ors.), has held thus:

sentences.text: The fact that the deceased was riding on a motor cycle along with the driver and another, may not, by itself, without anything more, make him guilty of contributory negligence.
At the most it would make him guilty of being a party to the violation of the law.
Section 128 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, imposes a restriction on the driver of a two wheeled motor cycle, not to carry more than one person on the motor cycle.
Section 194C inserted by the Amendment Act 32 of 2019, prescribes a penalty for violation of safety measures for motor cycle drivers and pillion riders.

Therefore,
the fact that a person was a pillion rider on a motor cycle along with the driver and one more person on the pillion, may be a violation of the law.

But such violation by itself, without anything more, cannot lead to a finding of contributory negligence,
unless it is established that his very act of riding along with two others, contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim.
There must either be a causal connection between the violation and the accident or a causal connection between the violation and the impact of the accident upon the victim.
It may so happen at times, that the accident could have been averted or the injuries sustained could have been of a lesser degree, if there had been no violation of the law by the victim.
What could otherwise have resulted in a simple injury, might have resulted in a grievous injury or even death due to the violation of the law by the victim.

It is in such cases, where, but for the violation of the law, either the accident could have been averted or the impact could have been minimized, that the principle of contributory negligence could be invoked.
It is not the case of the insurer that the accident itself occurred as a result of three persons riding on a motor cycle.
It is not even the case of the insurer that the accident would have been averted, if three persons were not riding on the motor cycle.

14. Coming to facts of present case, mere fact that petitioner was riding the motor cycle without having the driving licence and also driving the motor cycle along with two pillion riders will itself do not contribute or will not amounts to the rash and negligent driving only and until the respondents specifically proves that the petitioner was riding the motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner and thereby contributed to the cause of the accident.
Even RW-1 clearly admitted about the filing of the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
15. Apart from this, on perusal of the spot mahazar and sketch, spot of accident is a junction where cross road joins the main road and width of the road is 31 feet.

On perusal of Ex-P4 sketch,
admittedly the petitioner was riding the motor cycle on the main road from NAK Kalyana mantapa towards satellite bus stop.
Further the rider of the motor cycle was riding on the extreme left side of the road.
Further admittedly driver of the lorry was coming from the cross road i.e., from Subash publishing cross road and joining main road.
Ex-P4 clearly shows that when driver of the lorry was taking the right turn and joining the main road, at that point, the accident has been taken place.
Ex- P4 clearly demonstrate that when the driver of the lorry was taking right turn and joining the main road he must be cautious and slow looking into the moving traffic or vehicles on the main road.
Admittedly the vehicles which were coming from the cross road has to be cautious and after observing moving traffic on the main road has to cross the road and join the main road.

Ex-P4 clearly shows that driver of the lorry while turning right side to joint the main road has to take the Sampath Kumar Nagaraj vs H.S. Khiser Anjum on 2 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85442266/
5 wide right turn but in the present case, the driver of the lorry has taken the right turn in the narrow without observing for the traffic rules and vehicles moving on main road.

sentences.text: Thus it clearly shows that accident has been taken place due to the sole rash and negligence of the driver of the lorry.

The petitioner though was riding the motor cycle without driving licence and along with two pillion riders, but there is no evidence and materials coming on the record to show that the petitioner due to the triple riding has lost control over his vehicle and was riding the motor cycle in rash and negligently and due to which accident has been taken place.
Ex-P4 clearly shows that the petitioner was riding the motor cycle on the extreme left side.
It clearly shows that as the driver of the lorry has suddenly turn his lorry towards right side in a narrow way, hence accident has been taken place.
Admittedly driver of the lorry was joining the main road and was moving towards N.A.K.Kalyana mantapa i.e., right side of the main road.

Thus driver of the lorry has to take a wide right turn to move towards N.A.K.Kalyana mantapa, but as the driver of the lorry has taken the narrow right turn while joining the main road, accident has been taken place.
Ex-P4 clearly shows that the accident has been taken place due to the sole rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

16. Apart from this, the jurisdictional police after thorough and detailed investigation against the driver of the lorry bearing No.KA-53-C-4047 for the offence punishable u/s 279, 337, 338 of IPC 128 r/w 177, 3(1) r/w 181, 146 r/w 196 of IMV Act.

Though counsel for the respondent No.3 contended that police colluding with the petitioner has filed the charge sheet against the driver of the lorry, but no materials and evidence are placed on record to prove that the charge sheet filed by the police is wrong, defective and collusive.

Apart from this, though respondent contended that the accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the petitioner, but has not adduced evidence of any eye witness and also Investigation Officer to prove that Investigation Officer has falsely filed the charge sheet against the driver of the lorry.
Even respondent has not examined the driver of the lorry who is a material witness to state as to the facts and circumstances under which accident has been taken place.
The very non examination of the driver of the lorry is a fatal to the case of the prosecution.
Mere allegation is not sufficient, respondent has to prove the defence by placing cogent and reliable evidence and materials on record.
Even RW-1 legal manager of the company in his cross-examination clearly admitted that the charge sheet filed against the driver of the lorry and they have not challenging the charge sheet.

17. The filing of charge sheet in the Criminal case is prima-facie evidence for this case to prove that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of MGV bearing No.KA-53-C-4047.
18.

In fact, the proof of accident itself is sufficient for the purpose of this case, as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a decision reported in 2001 ACJ 1975 (Sri. Kumaresh V/s. The Divisional Manager, National Insurance Com. Ltd., and another)

entities.text: 2001 ACJ 1975 (Sri. Kumaresh V/s. The Divisional Manager, National Insurance Com. Ltd., and another)

sentences.text: , it was held in the above decision that, in the motor accident case strict proof of rash and negligent driving need not be established, as was required in criminal cases.
It is sufficient, if it is established that the claimant has sustained injuries as a result of the accident.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above decision and also prima-facie evidence produced by the petitioner, it is proved and established that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of MGV bearing No.KA-53-C- 4047 and the petitioners have sustained injuries due to RTA.

sentences.text: RW-1 pleaded his ignorance for the suggestion that driver of the lorry has pleaded guilty for offence charged against him and paid the fine.
If at all there was no rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry, certainly driver of the lorry would have contesting the case and would not have pleaded guilty.

19. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
20. Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the rider of offending vehicle.

21. In addenda, in a claim for compensation U/Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
22. ISSUE NO.2:-
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
23. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME:
So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 21 years.
The petitioner has produced the Adhaar card as per Ex.P.127, it disclose the date of birth of the petitioner as 5-5-1997 and the accident took place on 4-11-2017.
So, as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged 20 years 5 months 29 days.
The petitioner has stated that he was student, studying B pharma and actively participating in sports and other curricular activities.

Due to accidental injuries and prolonged period of treatment, he could not attend the class for the period of six months, unable to attend to examination, lost one valuable semester and missed his internals and valuable coaching for the said period and spent Rs.20,000/- for tuitions to coverup the classes of absent period.

As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : laceration over right parietal region measuring 4 cm x5 cms with stapled extend over right side of forehead measuring 5 cm in length, laceration over left corner of mouth to chin exposing fractured mandible, abrasion over left thigh measuring 5 cm x 2 cm,

It is needless to say that the said injury No.1 to 5 are grievous in nature.

Ex.P11 to 13-discharge summary discloses that for the aforesaid injuries, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient at St.John's medical college hospital from 4-11-2017 to 12-12-2017 and from4-2-2022 to 7-2-2022 for total period of 38 days.
25. It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr.Shailesh A.V.Rao as PW.3 who stated that petitioner had sustained injury to his head and lost consciousness, he was evaluated and admitted to St.John's medical college hospital, Bangalore and required intubation.
CT brain revealed frontal pneumocephalus, subarachnoid hemorrhage.
He also had fractures of orbit, frontal bone, maxillary sinus and mandible and underwent surgery for facio maxillary injuries.
He also underwent tracheostomy.
PW-3 further stated that skull x-ray was done on 25-11-2024.
this revealed implants over right frontal bone, mandible and maxilla.
Neuro psychological assessment was done on 29- 11-2024.
Patient IQ was 155(90-109)

On IDEAS, he obtained a score of 06,
suggestive of <40% disability.
MMSE was done on 30-11-2024.
He obtained a low score of 23/30.
PW-3 has assessed the disability of around 10% pertains to his wholebody and is likely to be permanent.
26. In the cross examination PW-3 clearly stated that in the CT scan, it is reported that there was a blood clot on the outer part of the brain and it will be curified through medicine.
Further PW-3 stated that petitioner has undergone facial surgery joints and throat portion.

Though PW-3 stated disability of around 10% to the PW-1, but PW-1 himself has appeared before this court and answers in cross examination rationally which shows that PW-1 was able to understand the questions and able to give answers in a rational way.
Moreover the way of answers given by PW-1 to question in cross-examination clearly shows that PW-1 is not suffering from any mental disability.
even PW-1 admitted that he has completed his B Pharmacy.
The very said fact on his completion of eduction establishes that there is no physical and mental disability.
Moreover petitioner was not doing any work and earning income as on the date of accident, hence there is no loss of future income.
Hence petitioner is not entitle for future loss of income.

sentences.text: Further petitioner took treatment at Trustwell Hospital from 4-2-2022 to 7-2-2022 for total period of 38 days.
PW-1 has stated that he is suffering from with whole physical and mental pain and agony and injuries sustained by him.
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner being 20 years and certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.
Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.
29. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES, INCIDENTAL CHARGES, LOSS OF INCOME TO THE PARENTS:

Admittedly as per the materials available on record, petitioner is residing in Krishnagiri Taluk, Tamilnadu and took treatment at St.John's medical college hospital, Bangalore as inpatient and certainly he would have hired the cab for traveling to the hospital.

Admittedly, petitioner has taken the treatment as inpatient for period of 38 days and undergone Stage 1 Arch bar+ ORIF of maxilla, mandible right body and left condylar fracture and resuturing of facial lacerations under GA on 16-11-2017 and ORIF right condyle, infraorbital rim+ orbital floor+ ZM buttress fracture fixation with 7th rib bone graft and titanium mesh done under GA on 25-11-2017

, certainly, it cannot be disputed that petitioner is dependent on the others and during the course of his treatment the petitioner might have spent more amount towards attendant charges, conveyance, extra nutritious food etc.
By considering the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner, petitioner would not have carried his routine works by himself and parents would have looked after him during his recovery.
The petitioner's parents could not have attended their work for those long period.
Therefore this Tribunal deems it expedient to take note of loss of income of parents during the course of treatment and rest of the petitioner.
Hence a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded under this head.
30. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS, LOSS OF MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.

Looking into age of petitioner, injuries sustained by petitioner and looking into his future marriage prospectus, the petitioner would obviously face depression, anxiety, disappointment & frustration and also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- is awarded under this head.
31. MEDICAL EXPENSES.
As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner got marked the document as per Ex.P.14 to 53 i.e.,medical bills for Rs.8,10,482/- and Ex-P54 to 122-prescriptions.
The bill No.3 to 40 are advance receipts and are included in final bill, hence they are not considered.

Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, the resultant disability suffered by him due to such injuries, I proceed to award Rs.5,07,752/- under the head of medical expenses.

33. INTEREST & LIABILITY: Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a., is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
34.
There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.3 being the insurer thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.3 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
35. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,57,752/- with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.3 is hereby directed to deposit total compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount to the petitioner, 40% shall be deposited in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to him through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on his deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

 Judgment
This is a petition filed u/s.166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, claiming for compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.
2. The petitioner's case in brief as follows:
Sampath Kumar Nagaraj vs H.S. Khiser Anjum on 2 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85442266/
2
opennyai_summary.facts:
The owner of the Honda Aciva intentionally entrusted/allowed 3 adult persons to travel on the honda activa on the road knowing fully well that the seating capacity of the honda activa is only 2, in the complaint, FIR, charge sheet and other police documents clearly reflects that at the time of accident there were three members were traveling on the honda activa.
The jurisdictional police have filed the charge sheet against the rider and owner of the honda activa bearing No.KA-53-H-8617.
Since there was no valid insurance policy to the honda activa, the jurisdictional police colluded with the petitioner has filed false charge sheet against the driver of the goods vehicle as A1 only with an intention to claim compensation by taking advantage of policy of insurance.
This respondent seeks protection u/s 147 & 149 of MV Act.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive.
The claim is bad for non compliance of section 158(6) and 134(c) of MV Act.
opennyai_summary.issue:
6. From the above said pleadings this tribunal has framed the following issues :
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the MVG bearing reg.No.KA-53-C- 4047 on 4-11-2017 at about 3.45 a.m. near rose wood international hotel, Timber yard layout,
Bengaluru ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate?
From whom?
3
. What Order or Award?
12. In the present case, charge sheet filed against the driver of the lorry for the offence punishable u/s 279, 338 of IPC and Charge sheet filed against the petitioner rider of the motor cycle for the offence punishable u/s 128 not for 279 of IPC.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
13. In this regard-The Hon'ble Apex Court in Civil Appeal No.79/2020 (Mohammed Siddiqui & Anr.,
v. National Insurance Co. Ltd., & Ors.), has held thus:
Sampath Kumar Nagaraj vs H.S. Khiser Anjum on 2 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85442266/
4
Therefore,
the fact that a person was a pillion rider on a motor cycle along with the driver and one more person on the pillion, may be a violation of the law.
But such violation by itself, without anything more, cannot lead to a finding of contributory negligence,
unless it is established that his very act of riding along with two others, contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim.
There must either be a causal connection between the violation and the accident or a causal connection between the violation and the impact of the accident upon the victim.
It may so happen at times, that the accident could have been averted or the injuries sustained could have been of a lesser degree, if there had been no violation of the law by the victim.
What could otherwise have resulted in a simple injury, might have resulted in a grievous injury or even death due to the violation of the law by the victim.
It is in such cases, where, but for the violation of the law, either the accident could have been averted or the impact could have been minimized, that the principle of contributory negligence could be invoked.
It is not the case of the insurer that the accident itself occurred as a result of three persons riding on a motor cycle.
It is not even the case of the insurer that the accident would have been averted, if three persons were not riding on the motor cycle.
14. Coming to facts of present case, mere fact that petitioner was riding the motor cycle without having the driving licence and also driving the motor cycle along with two pillion riders will itself do not contribute or will not amounts to the rash and negligent driving only and until the respondents specifically proves that the petitioner was riding the motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner and thereby contributed to the cause of the accident.
Even respondent has not examined the driver of the lorry who is a material witness to state as to the facts and circumstances under which accident has been taken place.
The very non examination of the driver of the lorry is a fatal to the case of the prosecution.
Mere allegation is not sufficient, respondent has to prove the defence by placing cogent and reliable evidence and materials on record.
In fact, the proof of accident itself is sufficient for the purpose of this case, as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a decision reported in 2001 ACJ 1975 (Sri. Kumaresh V/s. The Divisional Manager, National Insurance Com. Ltd., and another)
Sampath Kumar Nagaraj vs H.S. Khiser Anjum on 2 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85442266/
6 18.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
20. Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the rider of offending vehicle.
21. In addenda, in a claim for compensation U/Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.
There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.
However the respondent No.3 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, the resultant disability suffered by him due to such injuries, I proceed to award Rs.5,07,752/- under the head of medical expenses.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.3 being the insurer thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
35. ISSUE NO.3:
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,57,752/- with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.3 is hereby directed to deposit total compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount to the petitioner, 40% shall be deposited in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to him through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on his deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
